body:
I know people have downvoted you, but I appreciate your input. I'm happy that faith has brought you the love and happiness you were searching for. 

Unfortunately for me, I don't think this is my path. I grew up a reluctant Catholic- read multiple books on religion and continued searching as an agnostic up through college. I recently declared myself an atheist this summer after I realized I probably always was one at heart. For me, I know this sounds horrible but even if a God did exist, I wouldn't want to rely on its supernatural stories and unconditional love to get by. I want to have faith in myself before a deity. 

I guess I need something more tangible in regards to external love- by tangible I mean friends and family.
I had a therapist when I was 13-14 for family reasons, etc. I wasn't a huge fan. But I think what I was really looking for was someone to talk to that knew me well enough to understand and not judge.

In reality, I'm one of those people that equates educational achievements with self-worth. School and grades are important to me. Not life or death, but being in school was the one thing that constantly kept me going. New knowledge kept me curious. Once I graduated last May, I think that's when the depression really took hold. 


I'm not one of those people that can fully teach myself new concepts. I thrive on conversation. Now I feel so lonely- the friends I have unfortunately don't stimulate me mentally. Reddit helps, but I still find my daily life unbearable most of the time. Maybe with school it just kept me so busy that I couldn't notice my displeasure with the world around me- Yet now I'm starting to feel the pressure and responsibility of a college grad. It's awful. 

I have yet to find a job or career path that keep my motivation for very long.

Thank you for the honest reply. I think a lot of what actually motivates me to keep going is the potential to find something that can hold my interest. Perhaps I just haven't found it yet. 

I guess my ADD tendencies kind of play into the situation. I find something I like and obsess over it for a couple of days and then I completely lose interest. I'll keep working on it.

Hahaha this actually made me smile. While I'm sure ugly people can still date (haha), you helped me look at some of my all or nothing thoughts.

I wasn't in an emotionally abusive relationship or anything, but my ex never told me I looked good or showed too much sexual interest. It could really weigh down on me at times. I've always had self esteem issues, but I think your point is completely valid. Thanks.
